title: Can Knee Arthritis Be Reversed? Will It Keep Getting Worse?
metaDescription: Can knee arthritis be cured or reversed, and will it keep getting worse? An honest answer, plus what slows it down and what does not.
intro: Knee arthritis cannot be cured or reversed, but it does not always get worse. Many people stay steady for years, and some improve. What you do matters: exercise, a healthy weight and good pain control give your knee a good chance.

sections.heading: Can knee arthritis be cured?
sections.body: No. Both the NHS and Versus Arthritis say there is no cure. But treatment can ease pain and stiffness, and the condition does not necessarily get worse over time. Many people live well with it for years.

sections.heading: Will my knee keep getting worse?
sections.body: It varies. For some people the knee changes very little. For others it progresses faster. Symptoms often peak and then settle, with good days and bad days. Nobody can predict exactly, which is why we treat your symptoms, not just your X-ray.

sections.heading: Can anything slow it down?
sections.body: Staying active, keeping your thigh muscles strong, and reaching a healthy weight are the steps with the most supporting evidence. Versus Arthritis says treatment may slow the worsening. There is no tablet or injection that regrows the cushion in the knee.

sections.heading: Do supplements like glucosamine help?
sections.body: The evidence is weak. NICE advises against offering glucosamine, and the NHS no longer prescribes glucosamine or chondroitin. If you take them, do not rely on them to repair your knee.

sections.heading: What about injections and 'cartilage regrowth' treatments?
sections.body: Be careful with claims of regrowing cartilage. Steroid injections can give pain relief for several weeks to a few months, but they do not repair the knee. Your doctor can explain which injections may help your pain and which have little evidence.

sections.heading: What plan helps keep my knee going?
sections.body: Settle the pain with medicines, then exercise regularly, keep your weight in check, and use walking aids or physiotherapy treatments if needed. If pain still limits your life after a fair trial, ask about surgery. The choice is yours.

faqs.q: Is knee arthritis reversible with exercise?
faqs.a: Exercise does not reverse it, but it reduces pain and helps you move better.

faqs.q: Can knee arthritis go away on its own?
faqs.a: The damage does not go away, but symptoms can ease and stay settled for long periods.

faqs.q: Does knee arthritis spread to other joints?
faqs.a: No, it does not spread through the body, though a painful knee can put extra load on other joints.

faqs.q: Will I end up in a wheelchair?
faqs.a: Most people do not need surgery, according to the NHS, and treatment helps most people keep walking. If your knee does become very painful, surgery is an option.

faqs.q: Is knee arthritis just wear and tear?
faqs.a: Not simply. The joint is active and reacts; it is not just wearing out like a tyre. Normal activity does not cause it.
